title: Legislative districts of Calamba
wikitext:
{{Short description|Legislative district of the Philippines}} The '''legislative district of Calamba''' are the representations of the [[Cities of the Philippines|component city]] of [[Calamba, Laguna|Calamba]] in the [[Congress of the Philippines]]. The city is currently represented in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines|lower house]] of the Congress through its [[#Lone District|lone congressional district]]. == History == {{further|Legislative districts of Laguna}} Calamba was represented as part of the [[Legislative districts of Laguna#At-Large (defunct)|at-large district]] of Laguna in the [[Malolos Congress]] (1898–1899), [[National Assembly (Second Philippine Republic)|National Assembly of the Second Philippine Republic]] (1943–1944) and [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]] (1984–1986) and the [[Laguna's 1st congressional district|first district of Laguna]] from 1907 to 1941 and from 1945 to 1972. The province of Laguna was represented in the [[Interim Batasang Pambansa]] as part of [[Interim Batasang Pambansa#Regional Representatives|Region IV-A]] from 1978 to 1984, and elected [[Regular Batasang Pambansa#Members|four representatives]] at-large to the [[Regular Batasang Pambansa]] in [[1984 Philippine parliamentary election|1984]]. Calamba was placed in the [[Legislative districts of Laguna#1987–2019|second district]] of Laguna in accordance with the apportionment ordinance of the new [[Constitution of the Philippines|constitution]] which was proclaimed on February 11, 1987.{{cite web|author=1986 Constitutional Commission|title=1987 Constitution of the Philippines - Apportionment Ordinance|url=https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/constitutions/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines/the-1987-constitution-of-the-republic-of-the-philippines-ordinance/|date=February 11, 1987|access-date=May 9, 2019}} Calamba was separated from the second congressional district of Laguna by virtue of Republic Act No. 11078, which granted the city separate representation on September 24, 2018.{{cite web|url=https://www.officialgazette.gov.ph/2018/09/24/republic-act-no-11078/|title=Republic Act No. 11078 - An Act Separating the City of Calamba from the Second Legislative District of the Province of Laguna to constitute the Lone Legislative District of the City of Calamba|date=September 24, 2018|author=Congress of the Philippines|access-date=May 9, 2019}} The city elected its first representative in the [[2019 Philippine House of Representatives elections|2019 elections]]. Although Calamba is represented separately from the rest of Laguna in the [[House of Representatives of the Philippines]], the city's residents remain part of the province's [[Laguna Provincial Board|2nd ''Sangguniang Panlalawigan'' district]] for the purpose of electing ''[[Sangguniang Panlalawigan|SP]]'' members.{{cite web|url=http://www.comelec.gov.ph/?r=2019NLE/Resolutions/res10434|access-date=May 9, 2016|title=COMELEC Resolution No. 10434 - IN THE MATTER OF THE IMPLEMENTING RULES AND REGULATIONS OF REPUBLIC ACT NO. 11078 ENTITLED, "AN ACT SEPARATING THE CITY OF CALAMBA FROM THE SECOND LEGISLATIVE DISTRICT OF THE PROVINCE OF LAGUNA TO CONSTITUTE THE LONE LEGISLATIVE DISTRICT OF THE CITY OF CALAMBA"|author=Commission on Elections|date=October 15, 2018}} == Lone District == {{columns-list|colwidth=10em| {{legend|{{party color|Lakas–CMD}}|[[Lakas-CMD]] (1)|border=1px solid #aaaaaa}} }} {| class="wikitable sortable" style="margin: 1em auto; font-size:100%; line-height:20px; text-align:center" |+Legislative districts and representatives of [[Calamba, Laguna|Calamba]] !District ! colspan="3" |Current Representative !Party !Residency !Barangays !Population (2024) !Area |- ![[Calamba's at-large congressional district|Lone]] | style="background:{{party color|Lakas–CMD}};" | | [[File:Rep.
